summary: Moved paid-duel region eligibility to server-side determination at request time. Extracted an edge-compatible, headers-based core from paidDuelGeo.ts (decidePaidDuelGeo(GeoHeaderSource)) and a new single-source composer src/lib/rankedEligibility.ts (resolveRankedEligibility = PAID_DUELS_ENABLED kill switch + geo allow-list). /api/geo/ranked (edge) is now a thin wrapper over that helper, and app/duel/page.tsx and app/duel/chips/page.tsx resolve the same decision from next/headers headers() and pass it down as a required initialGeoAllowed prop. useRankedEligibility now takes a required server-derived seed and never starts at null, so the first paint carries the true decision and the available->UNAVAILABLE flash is gone. Verified from the next build route table that both pages flipped from static (o) to dynamic (f); added explicit export const dynamic = "force-dynamic" to both. Fail-closed posture, allow-list contents, GeoDecision shape, assertPaidDuelAllowed signature, and the /api/geo/ranked JSON shape are all unchanged. All six gates green. No dependencies added. Nothing committed or pushed.
goal: Server-side paid-duel region eligibility on /duel and /duel/chips: true region decision on first paint, no optimistic 'available' default, no flash; shared edge-compatible headers-based helper; fail-closed posture and PAID_DUELS_ENABLED / NEXT_PUBLIC_PAID_DUELS_ENABLED gating intact.

changes.what: Added exported interface GeoHeaderSource { get(name: string): string | null } and extracted decidePaidDuelGeo(headers: GeoHeaderSource): GeoDecision. assertPaidDuelAllowed(request) is now a one-line delegate, so its signature, return shape, allow-list contents, enforcementOn() semantics and all four existing callers are untouched. Module still has zero imports (pure, edge-safe).

NEW. resolveRankedEligibility(headers: GeoHeaderSource): { allowed: boolean; reason: 'disabled' | 'not_allowlisted' | 'missing_geo' | null }. Kill switch (PAID_DUELS_ENABLED) checked first, then decidePaidDuelGeo. Deliberately has NO 'enabled' parameter and no way to bypass either gate. No Node-only APIs, no next/* imports -> edge safe.

Now returns resolveRankedEligibility(request.headers) directly. runtime = 'edge' retained. JSON shape is byte-identical to before ({ allowed, reason }, reason 'disabled' when the kill switch is off, null when allowed) so the client contract did not change.

Now an async server component: resolveRankedEligibility(await headers()) -> <DuelHome initialGeoAllowed={allowed} />. Added export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'. Suspense boundary (needed by useSearchParams in DuelHome) preserved; metadata unchanged.
Same pattern -> <ChipDuelLobby initialGeoAllowed={allowed} />, plus export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'. metadata unchanged.

Signature is now useRankedEligibility(enabled: boolean, serverAllowed: boolean) and the returned allowed is boolean, never null. State is seeded from the server value and re-seeded via an effect when the prop changes (client-side nav reuses the component instance). The /api/geo/ranked fetch is kept strictly as revalidation, guarded with typeof data?.allowed === 'boolean' so a malformed body cannot clobber the server decision; a failed fetch keeps the server value.

Added required prop initialGeoAllowed: boolean (new DuelHomeProps interface). geoBlocked = paidEnabled && !geoAllowed (was `geoAllowed === false`, which was false during the null window). Everything else, including every other prop/export and the ModeCard presentational API, is untouched.

Added required prop initialGeoAllowed: boolean. Region-restricted branch is now `!geoAllowed` instead of `geoAllowed === false`, so the stake picker and 'Find match' (money-moving) UI can no longer render during an unresolved window.

openItemsForDownstream.message: There is no unit test yet for resolveRankedEligibility. I did not add one (verifier owns tests, and no gate required a missing file). It is not trivially testable in-process: PAID_DUELS_ENABLED is a module-level const in src/config/paidDuel.ts, so covering the 'disabled' branch needs vi.resetModules() + vi.stubEnv('PAID_DUELS_ENABLED', ...) followed by a dynamic import of src/lib/rankedEligibility. I deliberately did NOT add an injectable `enabled` parameter to keep the kill switch un-bypassable. PAID_DUEL_GEO_ENFORCE is read at call time, so the geo branches need no module reset.

learnings.insight: A jurisdictional gate rendered as `x === false` on a tri-state (null | true | false) client value is an allow-by-default. Both /duel and /duel/chips were STATICALLY PRERENDERED (verified: o in the HEAD build route table), so the HTML served to every region was a build-time shell showing chip duels as available, corrected only after a client fetch. The visible flash was the symptom; the real defect was that the default answer for a compliance gate was 'yes'.
learnings.action: For any compliance/eligibility gate, make the client state type `boolean`, not `boolean | null`, and require a server-derived seed as a REQUIRED prop/parameter. A required parameter makes 'render the gate without a server answer' unrepresentable instead of merely discouraged.

learnings.insight: Sharing request-derived logic between an edge route handler and a Next.js server component does not need a Request. Typing the helper against a minimal structural interface — `{ get(name: string): string | null }` — is satisfied by both a Headers object and next/headers' ReadonlyHeaders, with no next/* import in the shared module, so it stays edge-runtime safe.
learnings.action: When an API route and a server component must agree on a decision, extract the core against the narrowest structural input (headers, not Request) and keep the old Request-taking function as a one-line delegate. Existing callers and their tests then need zero changes.

learnings.insight: context/conventions.md's 'verify rendering mode from the next build route table, not by reasoning' paid off here: the intuition was that /duel was already dynamic (it renders a client component that fetches), but the build table proved it was `o` (static). A throwaway `git worktree add <scratch> HEAD --detach` plus a build in that worktree gives a clean before/after route table without stashing or touching the working tree.
learnings.action: When a change is supposed to alter Next.js rendering mode, capture the route table for BOTH HEAD and the working tree. Use a detached worktree in the scratchpad for the baseline — never git stash, which risks the in-progress work.

learnings.insight: Running `next build` in app/ rewrites the tracked file app/next-env.d.ts, flipping its references from ./.next/dev/types/* to ./.next/types/*. It shows up as an unrelated modified file in git status and would otherwise ride along in a commit.
learnings.action: After any `pnpm build` in app/, run `git checkout -- app/next-env.d.ts` and re-confirm `pnpm typecheck` before handing off. Do not commit that churn.

learnings.insight: Neither app/node_modules nor orchestrator/node_modules existed at the start of this session; all gates failed with misleading errors (TS2307 'Cannot find module vitest', 'tsx: not found') until deps were installed. app: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` (~11s) then `pnpm exec prisma generate`. orchestrator: `yarn install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`. A full `pnpm build` needs DATABASE_URL and DIRECT_URL set (any syntactically valid Postgres URL works — nothing connects at build time).
learnings.action: Install dependencies in both trees and run prisma generate before interpreting any gate failure. A TS2307 on a devDependency means missing node_modules, not a real type error.
